name: Shemer
title: The Owner of the Samaria Hill
summary: Shemer was the man who owned the hill where the city of Samaria was built. King Omri of Israel bought the hill from Shemer for two talents of silver and built there the new capital of Israel, which was named after Shemer.

keyEvents.title: The Sale of the Samaria Hill
keyEvents.description: Shemer sold the hill to King Omri of Israel for two talents of silver. Omri built a city on the hill and called it Samaria (Hebrew: Shomron) after Shemer, who had owned the hill.

keyEvents.title: Omri's Founding of Samaria
keyEvents.description: After buying from Shemer, Omri founded the city of Samaria, which became the capital of the Northern Kingdom and a political and religious center for several hundred years.

keyEvents.title: Samaria as Israel's Capital
keyEvents.description: The city built on Shemer's hill became the capital of the Northern Kingdom of Israel and remained so until the Assyrian conquest in 722 BC.

keyEvents.title: The Prophets' Warnings Against Samaria
keyEvents.description: The prophets repeatedly warned the inhabitants of Samaria, the city built on Shemer's hill, about coming judgment because of their sin and idolatry.

keyEvents.title: The Fall of Samaria to Assyria
keyEvents.description: The city built on Shemer's hill eventually fell to the Assyrians under King Salmanassar and Sargon II, and the people of Israel were taken into exile.
